deep.reconstruction:
The page has no mathematics. It is the verso of a small slip, written in pencil in two parts.

(1) A single large word in German cursive (Kurrent). The machine reading is 'Abschätzung' ('estimate'), with a question mark. The letter forms (A-b-long s-g/z-e-t-ung) are ambiguous. Other readings such as 'Absetzung' or a library or administrative term are possible. Given the context below, I would not read it as a mathematical heading.

(2) A bibliographic note in Latin script: 'Lamé Leçons sur la théorie math. de l'élasticité des corps solid.' This is G. Lamé, 'Leçons sur la théorie mathématique de l'élasticité des corps solides' (Paris, Bachelier, 1852).

Context: the recto (previous page) is a library borrowing or return slip. It lists Poggendorff's Annalen der Physik und Chemie, Dritte Reihe Bd. 29, and plates (Tafeln) to vols. 1-3, 7-9 and 10-12. It is marked 'Zurückerhalten' (returned), dated Febr. 25. [18]59, and signed B. Riemann with the address Weststraße. The mirror-image show-through of that recto is visible at left and lower right on this page. The next folio is Riemann's 1851 membership card for the Göttingen 'literarisches Museum'.

So this verso is most plausibly Riemann's reminder of a book to borrow or consult, Lamé's treatise on elasticity. That fits his documented 1850s interest in mathematical physics (elasticity, acoustics, his 1859 work on gas dynamics). No derivation, formula or computation is present, so nothing is reconstructed.

transcription_corrections: The first word is uncertain. 'Abschätzung' is not secure from the image, and a non-mathematical (library or administrative) word is equally plausible.
'corps solid.' is an abbreviation of 'corps solides'. The full title is 'Leçons sur la théorie mathématique de l'élasticité des corps solides' (Lamé, 1852).
The faint mirrored text at left and lower right is show-through from the recto library slip (Poggendorff Annalen ... Bd. 1-3, 7-9, 10-12) and is not part of this page's content.
